checks_by_claim.source_location: Lemma 2 PDF pp.7–8; Corollary 3(ii) p.10; Theorem 1(iii) pp.26–30
checks_by_claim.verification: For arbitrary integer K>=32, choose k=K and the least prime p>k^(Kk), so Bertrand gives p<2k^(Kk). Set m=4k+4,i=m-1,y=p^(1/m),x=ceil(y). Then y>k^(K/8)>=k^4>k and x^i/p<=exp(i/y)/y<2/y<1. The negative endpoint branch forces all numbers -kx-2kx sum_(ell=1)^(i-1)x^ell+sum_(ell=0)^(i-1)delta_ell x^ell with 0<=delta_ell<=k into A_i and hence A. Base-x digits are distinct and their total spread is less than x^i<p, so no modular collisions occur. Consequently |A|>=(k+1)^(4k+3)>2k^(K/2)>p^(1/(2k+2)). Enlarging any proposed real universal constant to an integer cannot fix the family.
checks_by_claim.impact: This invalidates the printed construction's necessary quantitative input to the proof of Theorem B. It is not merely an A1/C_i subscript objection.
checks_by_claim.counterexample_scope: The existential small-set lemma and Theorem B are not themselves disproved. No alternative construction or complete changed-threshold theorem has been established.
checks_by_claim.severity_reason: The failed construction supplies a necessary core estimate; Major remains justified.

checks_by_claim.source_location: Lemma 1 PDF pp.5–6; Corollary 1 p.7; Appendix p.39
checks_by_claim.verification: With the intended nonempty convention S1(3)=3 and S1(7)=5, contradicting the claimed 2 floor(log2 p). The p=7 lower bound follows by translating/scaling a three-term progression to -1,0,1: a fourth point would have to belong to both {2,3} and {4,5}. The corrected bound 2 floor(log2 p)+2 handles the power-of-two boundary; for p>=512 its square is below p-1. The remaining specified primes are covered by the finite Appendix sets, independently rechecked by the native auxiliary.
checks_by_claim.counterevidence: This repairs the sufficient small-set input for Theorem A.
checks_by_claim.limit: Optimality through 151 and necessity for every excluded prime were not exhaustively redone; no claim beyond the sufficient-condition repair.

checks_by_claim.source_location: Propositions 2–3 PDF pp.16–17; Lemmas 6–7 and actual main use
checks_by_claim.verification: For p=5,n=1,M=[1], the printed hyperplanes are singletons, forcing f=g=0, so their universal pairing condition is true; but x=1 has Mx=1 nowhere zero and (1-g)^2 is nonzero in both relevant group rings. Correct coordinate-line sums give the intended frequency-hyperplane vanishing. The bilinear Parseval formula includes ghat(-u); these hyperplanes are closed under negation. Over Fp, the translation-difference image/kernel and adjoint argument proves the corrected equivalence.
checks_by_claim.impact: The auxiliary equivalences are genuinely false, but the main induction uses the independently valid Lemma 7 coefficient identity. No core failure is inferred from these local propositions.

checks_by_claim.verification: The missing p^-n Fourier factor, signs from I-translation, finite-field power sums, point indicators and coefficient pairings are nonzero units. All actually used zero/nonzero tests survive. The (p-1)^n wording denotes dimension. No necessary derivation is invalidated by these units, so the literal corrections remain as normalisation/notation clarification without substantive Minor count.

The allowed p=5,M=I2,r=s=(4,1) gives Q=5. The target coefficient is 1, while the intermediate coefficient is 5=0 and Q!=0 in F5, making the printed division undefined. A valid proof sums over nonnegative matrices ell_ij with fixed row/column sums, dividing only by ell_ij!, where ell_ij<=p-1. The two coefficients are (product r_i!)H and (product s_j!)H, proving the required zero equivalence. Equivalently the weighted identity may first be proved integrally and then reduced.
checks_by_claim.impact: A local proof qualification is necessary on an admitted endpoint; the duality conclusion remains true. No claim to have rerun the historical 40,800 finite comparisons.
